source.title: Depersonalization/Derealization Disorder and Neural Correlates of Trauma-related Pathology

confidence_rationale: Closest available clinical existence-proof of MECH-524's restrictive pole read literally: a person whose stress-response capacity is intact or hyperactive, yet whose engagement with self/world content does not resume. Held at moderate-low confidence because depersonalization/derealization disorder is a tonic, global, trait-like detachment state, not the episodic per-goal reseeding failure MECH-524's trigger is specified as, and a narrative single-author review is weaker source quality than a meta-analysis.
failure_signatures: DPDR's detachment is typically tonic and trait-like across the entire self-world relationship, not an episodic per-goal reseeding failure. If MECH-524's dissociative pole in REE were similarly tonic -- a general dampening of the spare-compute trigger across ALL parked entries rather than a per-entry mis-trigger -- that would be a different, and arguably more concerning, failure mode, and the falsifier design in MECH-524's own notes does not yet distinguish 'this one entry never got reseeded' from 'the trigger itself is globally suppressed.'

The review explicitly notes DPDR's precise neurocircuit-to-symptom mapping remains incompletely resolved even for the human clinical case. Citing it grounds the EXISTENCE and clinical plausibility of a capacity-present/engagement-absent phenotype, not a specific implementable trigger-failure mechanism.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Depersonalization and derealization are estranged states of detachment from self and surroundings respectively, ranging from a transient normal reaction to trauma up to a persistent, highly debilitating disorder (DPDR). Involves adaptive stress-response circuitry (autonomic function, HPA axis, defense cascades) but recent evidence implicates more complex mechanisms including emotional dysregulation and disintegration of the body schema. DPDR is not merely a disruption of sensory integration but a disruption of several large-scale brain networks.
mapping.ree_translation: DPDR is the closest available clinical instance of MECH-524's restrictive-trigger pole read literally: capacity is not absent (stress-response and autonomic systems are, if anything, engaged rather than incapacitated in many DPDR presentations), yet engagement with the self, world, and ongoing personally-relevant content the person would ordinarily be invested in does not resume. This is close to a direct clinical existence-proof of the specific failure mode MECH-524's notes describe -- 'indistinguishable from an entry that was never worth resuming': a DPDR patient is not unable to act, but the affective/motivational stamp that would normally trigger re-engagement is disconnected from otherwise-intact processing capacity.
mapping.mapping_caveat: DPDR is a global, tonic, trait-like clinical state (detachment from self AND world, continuously), not an episodic, per-goal reseeding failure the way MECH-524's trigger is specified (spare-compute or sleep-entry gated re-seeding of ONE specific interruption_snapshot). Mapping a global disorder onto a per-entry mechanism risks over-claiming -- the honest reading is that DPDR shows the general phenomenon (capacity present, engagement absent) is a real, well-documented clinical category, not that DPDR patients specifically fail at the narrow reseeding operation MECH-524 proposes.
mapping.source_context: Narrative/mechanistic clinical-neuroscience review synthesizing neurocircuit and large-scale-network findings specifically in depersonalization/derealization disorder, framed around trauma-related pathology rather than DPDR epidemiology or treatment.

confidence_components.notes: Mid-tier clinical neuroscience journal, single-author narrative review rather than a meta-analysis or primary data -- chosen over the higher-circulation general DPDR reviews found in the same search (Wilkhoo et al. 2024 in a lower-tier journal; Salami et al. 2020, EEG-specific) because it is explicitly framed around neural-network disintegration rather than symptom epidemiology or treatment, which is the more mechanistically relevant framing for MECH-524. The tonic/global-vs-episodic/per-entry mismatch noted in mapping_caveat caps mapping_fidelity at moderate despite the phenomenon being a strong conceptual match. A systematic or meta-analytic DPDR neuroimaging review would improve on this entry if a dedicated future pull wants to strengthen it further.
